usageNotes: Removes a network interface configuration from the node's network config file (`/etc/network/interfaces`). The change is staged — it takes effect only after applying the pending network configuration (see `put_nodes_node_network`). Use the `digest` parameter to guard against concurrent edits when multiple operators may be modifying network config simultaneously.

examples.summary: Delete a bridge interface named vmbr1 from node pdm01

destructiveReason: Permanently removes the named interface from the node's network configuration; any VMs or services bound to that interface lose their network path once the configuration is applied.
tips: The deletion is not applied until you call PUT /nodes/{node}/network to commit pending network changes; the node continues using the old config until then.
Fetch the current digest via GET /nodes/{node}/network before deleting to pass a valid SHA256 digest and prevent race conditions.
Requires System.Modify privilege scoped to the specific interface path; token-based auth is supported.
Attempting to delete an interface that is still referenced by a VM NIC or another interface (e.g., a bond slave) may cause errors or network disruption after apply — verify dependencies first.
